name: Battle of Guandu
note: The plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: the formations are armies and detachments, and the places are towns and a river. Positions are schematic. Yangwu lay directly north of Guandu and Wuchao lay near Gushi, 40 li from Guandu; the accounts do not say on which side, so Gushi and Wuchao are placed to the north-west by judgement.

phases.title: The armies face each other
phases.text: Yuan Shao's army came to Yangwu, directly north of Guandu, and began building earthen fortifications. Cao Cao's troops held Guandu, where they had prepared fortifications.
phases.quote: Yuan Shao's army pushed to Yangwu (陽武; near present-day Yuanyang County, Henan), directly north of Guandu, and began constructing earthen fortifications.

phases.title: Yuan Shao advances into trench warfare
phases.text: Yuan Shao's army moved slowly south from Yangwu and fought Cao Cao's men in trench warfare, from behind earthen embankments that both sides made around their positions.
phases.quote: Yuan Shao's army slowly advanced southward from Yangwu and engaged Cao Cao's men in trench warfare, behind the earthen embankments that both sides made.

phases.title: Siege engines and tunnels at Guandu
phases.text: Yuan Shao raised siege ramps and high platforms to shoot arrows onto Cao Cao's men, who answered with traction trebuchets that destroyed the platforms. A ditch dug within Cao Cao's lines blocked Yuan Shao's tunnels, and neither side overcame the other.
phases.quote: Yuan Shao had erected siege-ramps and high platforms which allowed his men to rain arrows onto Cao Cao's forces. In response, Cao Cao's men had to carry their shields above their heads, and retaliated with traction trebuchets that destroyed the archer platforms. Yuan Shao also tried to tunnel under Cao Cao's fort, but Cao Cao had a large ditch dug within his lines to block the tunnels.

phases.title: Cavalry raid the grain depot at Gushi
phases.text: Cao Cao sent small cavalry units under Xu Huang and Shi Huan against the depot at Gushi, where Han Meng guarded Yuan Shao's grain. Han Meng was routed and the grain carts were burnt.
phases.quote: They succeeded, routing Han Meng, disrupting Yuan Shao's supply lines, and burning his grain carts.

phases.title: Supplies reach Wuchao and Cao Cao sets out
phases.text: Chunyu Qiong brought an army of 10,000 with large food reserves to Wuchao. That night Cao Cao and Yue Jin took 5,000 infantry and cavalry from Guandu to attack it, leaving Cao Hong and Xun You in charge of the main camp.
phases.quote: Thus at night, Cao Cao and Yue Jin led 5,000 infantry and cavalry to attack Wuchao after leaving Cao Hong and Xun You in charge of his main camp at Guandu.

phases.title: Wuchao's defences are overrun and its forts burn
phases.text: Cao Cao's army, disguised as a reinforcement unit from Yuan Shao, attacked Wuchao. Chunyu Qiong's first defences were overrun, and he fell back to his forts, which Cao Cao attacked and set on fire.
phases.quote: Chunyu Qiong's initial defences were overrun, and he retreated to hold his forts, which Cao Cao attacked and set on fire.

phases.title: Yuan Shao sends his main army against Guandu
phases.text: Zhang He urged help for Wuchao, but Guo Tu urged an attack on Guandu. Yuan Shao sent Zhang He and Gao Lan with his main army against Cao Cao's camp, and only a small cavalry unit to Wuchao. Cao Cao held his men at Guandu.
phases.quote: Yuan Shao used Guo Tu's idea and sent Zhang He and Gao Lan to lead his main army to attack Cao Cao's main camp at Guandu, while only sending a small cavalry unit to reinforce Wuchao.

phases.title: Wuchao is taken and its supplies burn
phases.text: The raid on Wuchao inflicted over a thousand casualties. Yue Jin captured Chunyu Qiong, and almost all of Yuan Shao's food supplies there were burnt.
phases.quote: Chunyu Qiong was captured by Yue Jin and had his nose cut off. Almost all of Yuan Shao's food supplies at Wuchao were burnt.

phases.title: Zhang He and Gao Lan surrender at Guandu
phases.text: Zhang He and Gao Lan failed to break through Cao Cao's lines at Guandu. After the news from Wuchao they surrendered to Cao Hong and destroyed their weapons.
phases.quote: Zhang He and Gao Lan surrendered to Cao Hong and destroyed their weapons.

phases.title: Cao Cao attacks Yuan Shao's army
phases.text: Cao Cao's forces seized the opportunity and launched a full attack on Yuan Shao's army, whose men were already shaken by the loss of their supplies.
phases.quote: Cao Cao's forces seized the opportunity to launch the full attack on Yuan's army.

phases.title: Yuan Shao flees north across the river
phases.text: Yuan Shao's army was destroyed and much of its supplies were captured. Yuan Shao fled north across the Yellow River with about 800 cavalry, which was what was left of his army.
phases.quote: Yuan Shao himself fled north across the Yellow River with only about 800 cavalry, which was what was left of his army.
